is the way to decide whether to offer "Paste". The answer is a hint —
content may change before you read it.

members.summary: Open a surface `lingxia.yaml` declares.
members.description:
Open a surface `lingxia.yaml` declares. Without options it opens with the declaration's own
placement; `key`, `as` and `edge` change shared shell composition and are
the Control app's.

signatures.text: openDeclared(id: string, options?: OpenDeclaredOptions): Promise<DeclaredSurface | AppSurface>

throws.when: `lingxia.yaml` declares no such surface.
`key`, `as` or `edge` from an lxapp other than the Control app, or a declared app is taken down; `reason` is `'appUnderMaintenance'` or `'appSuspended'`.
It is the root main surface and cannot change role.
A `key` on a surface that is not a declared native one.

members.summary: Open one of this lxapp's pages as a float or a window.
members.description:
Open one of this lxapp's pages as a float or a window. Returns at once;
await `.opened` to wait for the page.

signatures.text: openPage<N extends ConfiguredPageName>(page: N, ...options: OpenPageArgs<N>): PageSurface<NavResult<N>, NavMessages<N>>

throws.when: Malformed options.
`as: 'window'` where the host has no windows; `reason` is `'placementUnsupported'`.
A page the app does not declare.

examples:
const sheet = lx.surface.openPage('settings', { as: 'float' });
await sheet.opened;

members.summary: Open a URL in the in-app browser, as a main tab or docked as an aside.
members.description: Open a URL in the in-app browser, as a main tab or docked as an aside.

signatures.text: openUrl(url: string | URL, options?: OpenUrlOptions): Promise<TabSurface>

throws.when: A URL that is not a string or `URL`, an unknown option, or an `edge` without `as: 'aside'`.
The browser could not open it.

members.summary: Dialogs, action sheets and toasts.
members.description: Dialogs, action sheets and toasts.

members.summary: Shows a list of actions.
members.description:
Shows a list of actions.
Resolves `{ status: 'ok', id }` when the user selects an item; `id` identifies the selected item. Resolves `{ status: 'canceled' }` only when the
user dismisses the sheet. Rejects when presentation fails or the host returns
an invalid selection.

throws.when: `signal` aborted; the sheet is closed.
An empty or repeated id, an empty label, no items, or an unknown `tone`.
No page can show a sheet now; `reason` is `'appClosed'` when the app is not open.

members.summary: Acknowledgement-only dialog.
members.description: Acknowledgement-only dialog. Resolves when the user dismisses it.

throws.when: `signal` aborted; the dialog is closed.
No page can show a dialog now; `reason` is `'appClosed'` when the app is not open.
The dialog could not be shown.

members.summary: Ask a yes/no question.
members.description: Ask a yes/no question. Dismissal resolves false; presentation failure rejects.

throws.when: `signal` aborted; the dialog is closed.
No page can show a dialog now; `reason` is `'appClosed'` when the app is not open.
The dialog could not be shown.

members.summary: Show a short message over the page.
members.description: Show a short message over the page. Returns at once; a newer toast replaces it.

throws.when: The app is not open; `reason` is `'appClosed'`.

members.summary: Leave, with `value` as the opener's result.
members.description:
Leave, with `value` as the opener's result. A pushed page goes back; a
surface page closes its surface. Throws for a root or tab page, or a
pushed page that is not on top, and while `setup` runs.

members.description:
The size class this page lays out for. `watch` delivers it at once, then
when `sizeClass` or `canDock` changes (not on every resize), and stops
when the page unloads.

members.description:
Follow it, starting with the current value; returns an unsubscribe. The

types.description:
Launch-at-startup control for the host app.
Wherever the host cannot register a startup item every call fails
`E_NOT_SUPPORTED`; ask first:
```ts
if (lx.supports('host.autostart')) {
// render the "Launch at startup" toggle
}
```
Requires `capabilities.autostart: true` in `lingxia.yaml`; without it
`lx.supports` says no on all platforms. Declaring the capability never enables
autostart by itself — the SDK registers the app only when `enable()`
is called, so the decision stays with the user (typically a settings-page
toggle, default off).
Host-app-level capability: like `update.check` and `screenshot`, the methods
are available only to the native-assigned Control app; other lxapps receive
a permission error.

types.name: BannerApi
types.summary: Product-drawn desktop banner, top-right.
types.description:
Product-drawn desktop banner, top-right. Not an OS notification and
not bound to App Link. Desktop only, in every lxapp: elsewhere every
call fails `E_NOT_SUPPORTED`, so ask `lx.supports('host.banner')` first.
Needs no `capabilities` entry in `lingxia.yaml`. The card is 328 pt wide.
A guest lxapp's banner carries its name and icon, so
it cannot pass as the product's. Its ids are its own, it may have
three banners showing or waiting, each closes after 60s at most
(`durationMs` is capped), and the product's banners go first.

types.name: NotificationApi
types.summary: Local notifications as a resume affordance.
types.description:
Local notifications as a resume affordance.
Without `capabilities.notifications`, or where the platform has no
local API, every call fails `E_NOT_SUPPORTED`; ask
`lx.supports('host.notification')` first.
Declaring the capability never prompts; permission runs on
`lx.device.permission.request('notifications')` or the first `show()`
that reaches the OS.
Every lxapp may call it. The Control app speaks for the product; a
guest lxapp speaks only for itself: its ids are its own (it cannot
replace or cancel another app's), a tap can only open itself, it
may hold 32 live notifications, and it may cause at most one
permission prompt per launch, only while it is open on screen.

surface page closes its surface. Throws for a root or tab page, or a
pushed page that is not on top, and while `setup` runs.

Show the refresh indicator and run `onRefresh`, as a pull would.

`enablePullDownRefresh`, or `'pageUnloaded'` once the page has unloaded.

fields.name: orientation
fields.summary: Lock the window to `portrait` or `landscape` while this page is current.
fields.description:
Lock the window to `portrait` or `landscape` while this page is current.
The lock beats `pageOrientation`; only a full-screen video beats it. It
ends when the page unloads, so the next page gets its own orientation.
`lock` throws `E_INVALID_ARG` for any other value.

fields.description:
The size class this page lays out for. `watch` delivers it at once, then
when `sizeClass` or `canDock` changes (not on every resize), and stops
when the page unloads.

away, or a newer result promise replaced this one), `reclaimed` (a
hidden surface page unloaded under memory pressure), `app_closed`.

fields.description:
Leave the page; rejects for a pushed page that is not on top. Called
before `opened` settles, it stops the open instead.

fields.description:

into declarative UI; for event-driven updates use `onShow` / `onHide`.

Live rather than a snapshot: a later open that moves the surface, or the
user dragging it, updates the handle you already hold.
Where it is shown.

fields.description:
Restore a hidden surface. The page instance survived, so scroll
position, form input, and JS state come back with it. Idempotent.

fields.name: hide
fields.summary: Hide without destroying.
fields.description:
Hide without destroying. Main surfaces cannot be hidden and reject.
Idempotent.

fields.name: file
fields.summary: Picks one file.
fields.description:
Picks one file. Resolves `{ status: 'canceled' }` only when the user
dismisses the picker, otherwise `{ status: 'ok', file }`.

throws.when: A `defaultPath` outside lxapp storage.
`signal` aborted.
The picker failed or returned a file the lxapp cannot read.

fields.name: files
fields.summary: Picks one or more files.
fields.description:
Picks one or more files. Resolves `{ status: 'canceled' }` only when the
user dismisses the picker, otherwise `{ status: 'ok', files }`.

throws.when: A `defaultPath` outside lxapp storage.
`signal` aborted.
The picker failed or returned a file the lxapp cannot read.

fields.name: directory
fields.summary: Ask the person for a folder; resolves `canceled` only when they dismiss the picker.
fields.description:
Ask the person for a folder; resolves `canceled` only when they dismiss the picker.
The picked `path` is a read-only root that `lx.fs` reads and `lx.fs.copy`
take as `<path>/<relative>`, each segment percent-encoded; nothing outside
it resolves, including through a symlink.

platform: Android, HarmonyOS phones and tablets: no system folder picker, so only a `defaultPath` in lxapp storage works.

throws.when: No system folder picker and `defaultPath` is not in lxapp storage.
`signal` aborted.

fields.name: media
fields.summary: Lets the person get pictures and videos from where they choose: the library, the camera, or either, asked first in a host-drawn sheet.
fields.description:
Lets the person get pictures and videos from where they choose: the library, the camera, or
either, asked first in a host-drawn sheet. Library items are copied to temp on mobile; desktop
returns the user's file. For one camera item with set options, see `lx.pick.capture`;
compression is `lx.media.compressImage`. Resolves `{ status: 'canceled' }` when the person
dismisses the sheet, picker or camera, otherwise `{ status: 'ok', files }`.

throws.when: A `sources` or `types` entry outside its union, or an empty `sources`.
Only the camera on a host without `pick.camera`; with the library, such a host opens the library without asking.
`signal` aborted; the source sheet is closed.
The picker failed or returned an invalid payload.

fields.name: capture
fields.summary: Takes one photo or records one video with the camera, with these settings.

types.name: SurfaceApi
types.summary: Surfaces beside or above the page stack, each with a handle.

fields.name: openPage
fields.type: <N extends ConfiguredPageName>(page: N, ...options: OpenPageArgs<N>) => PageSurface<NavResult<N>, NavMessages<N>>
fields.summary: Open one of this lxapp's pages as a float or a window.
fields.description:
Open one of this lxapp's pages as a float or a window. Returns at once;
await `.opened` to wait for the page.

throws.when: Malformed options.
`as: 'window'` where the host has no windows; `reason` is `'placementUnsupported'`.
A page the app does not declare.

fields.name: openUrl
fields.summary: Open external content in the in-app browser.
fields.description: Open external content in the in-app browser.

fields.name: openApp
fields.summary: Open another lxapp in main or a companion slot, focus it if it is open, or move it to the role `as` names.
fields.description:
Open another lxapp in main or a companion slot, focus it if it is open,
or move it to the role `as` names. Control app only.

fields.name: openDeclared
fields.summary: Open a surface the host declared in `lingxia.yaml`, with the placement the declaration chose.
fields.description:
Open a surface the host declared in `lingxia.yaml`, with the placement
the declaration chose. `key`, `as` and `edge` (Control app only) open a
keyed instance or override the placement; `as` and `edge` also move a
live instance. A declaration that shows an lxapp resolves to that app's
`AppSurface`.

fields.name: get
fields.summary: Find one of this lxapp's own live pages or browser tabs by the key passed to `openPage` / `openUrl`.
fields.description:
Find one of this lxapp's own live pages or browser tabs by the key passed
to `openPage` / `openUrl`. Declared surfaces and other lxapps are found
with `lx.surface.declared` and `lx.surface.app`.

fields.name: app
fields.summary: The handle of an lxapp live as a surface of its own, declared or not; `undefined` when it is not.
fields.description:
The handle of an lxapp live as a surface of its own, declared or not;
`undefined` when it is not. Control app only.

fields.name: declared
fields.type: (id: string, options?: GetDeclaredOptions) => DeclaredSurface | AppSurface | undefined
fields.summary: The handle of a live declared surface, or of its keyed instance, the same object on every call; `undefined` when it is not live.
fields.description:
The handle of a live declared surface, or of its keyed instance, the same
object on every call; `undefined` when it is not live. Control app only.

types.name: SurfaceBase
types.summary: What every surface handle carries, whatever opened it.
types.description: What every surface handle carries, whatever opened it.

fields.name: kind
fields.summary: Which kind of surface this is; narrows the handle.
fields.description: Which kind of surface this is; narrows the handle.

fields.name: key
fields.summary: The caller-supplied identity, when this surface was opened with one.
fields.description: The caller-supplied identity, when this surface was opened with one.

fields.name: realized
fields.summary: The placement the host produced, which an ordered preference may narrow.
fields.description:
The placement the host produced, which an ordered preference may narrow.
Live rather than a snapshot: a later open that moves the surface, or the
user dragging it, updates the handle you already hold.

fields.name: alive
fields.summary: True until `close()` fires; afterwards the page instance is torn down.
fields.description: True until `close()` fires; afterwards the page instance is torn down.

fields.name: visible
fields.summary: Last-known visibility, kept in sync with the native side.
fields.description:
Last-known visibility, kept in sync with the native side. Safe to bind
into declarative UI; for event-driven updates use `onShow` / `onHide`.

fields.name: close
fields.summary: Destroy the surface.
fields.description:
Destroy the surface. The stable root main cannot be closed. Repeated
calls after a successful close are idempotent.

fields.name: onClose
fields.summary: Fires once when the surface closes, whoever closed it.
fields.description: Fires once when the surface closes, whoever closed it. Returns a function that removes the handler.

types.name: SurfaceCloseReason
types.summary: Why a surface closed.
types.description: Why a surface closed.

types.name: SurfaceClosedEvent
types.summary: What a surface's `onClosed` receives.
types.description: What a surface's `onClosed` receives.

fields.name: reason
fields.summary: Why it closed.
fields.description: Why it closed.

types.name: SurfaceEdge
types.summary: Preferred docking side for an aside when the Host has room for a docked layout.
types.description:
Preferred docking side for an aside when the Host has room for a docked
layout. `aside` selects the companion region; `edge` selects a side within
it. Compact Hosts may reproject the same aside as a full-screen overlay.

types.name: SurfaceFloatPosition
types.summary: Where a float popup anchors (default `center`).
types.description: Where a float popup anchors (default `center`).

types.name: SurfaceInteraction
types.summary: Native interaction supplied by the host around page content.
types.description: Native interaction supplied by the host around page content.

fields.name: closeButton
fields.summary: Show the standard circular close button.
fields.description: Show the standard circular close button.

fields.name: dismiss
fields.summary: Whether a tap outside closes it.
fields.description: Whether a tap outside closes it.

fields.name: modal
fields.summary: Block interaction with content below.
fields.description: Block interaction with content below.

types.name: SurfaceKind
types.summary: Where the content came from.
types.description:
Where the content came from. The discriminant on every surface
handle, so `AnySurface` narrows without a runtime `typeof` check.

types.name: SurfaceMessaging
types.summary: Two-way messaging, available when both sides are lxapp pages.
types.description: Two-way messaging, available when both sides are lxapp pages.

fields.name: send
fields.summary: Sends to the other side: from the opener to the opened page, from the page (`page.surface`) to its opener.
fields.description:
Sends to the other side: from the opener to the opened page, from the
page (`page.surface`) to its opener. Delivered at once and uncopied to
the other side's `onMessage` handlers; until it first subscribes,
messages wait for it.

fields.name: onMessage
fields.summary: Receives what the other side sends.
fields.description: Receives what the other side sends. Returns a function that removes the handler.

types.name: SurfacePlacement
types.summary: What the host actually produced.
types.description:
What the host actually produced. Reported by `realized`, which is
how a caller reads the outcome of an ordered placement preference.

types.name: SurfaceShowable
types.summary: Surfaces the host can hide and restore without losing page state.
types.description: Surfaces the host can hide and restore without losing page state.

fields.name: show
fields.summary: Restore a hidden surface.
fields.description:
Restore a hidden surface. The page instance survived, so scroll
position, form input, and JS state come back with it. Idempotent.

fields.name: hide
fields.summary: Hide without destroying.
fields.description:
Hide without destroying. Main surfaces cannot be hidden and reject.
Idempotent.

fields.name: onShow
fields.summary: Fires on a real transition to visible, whichever side drove it.
fields.description: Fires on a real transition to visible, whichever side drove it.

fields.name: onHide
fields.summary: Fires on a real transition to hidden, whichever side drove it.
fields.description: Fires on a real transition to hidden, whichever side drove it.

types.name: SurfaceVisibilityEvent
types.summary: Detail payload for `onShow` / `onHide` events.
types.description:
Detail payload for `onShow` / `onHide` events. `source` identifies which
Surface object initiated the visibility change so observers can

types.name: UploadOptions
types.summary: Upload options.
types.description:
Upload options. The file streams from disk, so the size ceiling is
the remote's, not memory.
`bodyMode` picks the body shape, and with it which of the other
fields apply:
- `multipart` (default) wraps the file in a `multipart/form-data`
envelope beside the `fields` text fields — what an ordinary form
endpoint parses. `field`, `fileName`, and `fields` describe that
envelope. `fields`, when present, must contain at least one entry.
- `raw` sends the file bytes as the entire body. Presigned
object-storage URLs (S3, OSS, Azure Blob) need this: a multipart
envelope would be stored verbatim as the object's contents,
boundary lines and all. `field`, `fields`, and `fileName` are
then rejected rather than silently dropped.

extends the page to the window edge while keeping the system
minimize, maximize, resize, and drag affordances — the runtime owns

to opt in still cannot trap the user.
